scope: Korean names and concise editorial meaning clues for the 206 canonical radical-number groups used by this site. Traditional names and shape names are not all standalone-character readings.

sources.title: 국립국어원 2016-01-32 · 점자 활용 규격 표준화 및 사용자별 교육 과정 개발: 유니코드 표준을 고려한 점자·점형 체계 표준화 연구
이젠교육 고등학교 한문 교사용 자료 · 부록 3. 부수 일람표

editorialPolicy: Names were transcribed from the Korean references, normalized for spacing, and where helpful selected from documented classroom shape-name variants. Meaning fields are short editorial Korean explanations, not an official HSK translation or an automatic rule for semantic/phonetic roles. Facts such as names, readings, and basic lexical meaning clues are retained; the source tables and prose are not reproduced.

importantDistinctions.20: 쌀 포 uses the Korean verb 싸다, to wrap; it does not mean rice 쌀.
importantDistinctions.90: 장수장변 is a conventional radical shape-name; the meaning clue 쪼갠 나무 describes the wood-half form rather than translating the name literally.
importantDistinctions.129: 오직 율 is a recorded traditional name; 붓 율 is retained as a meaning/reading alias. The meaning clue is 붓.
importantDistinctions.58: 튼가로왈 is a conventional shape-name, not a claim that the standalone character is pronounced 왈.
importantDistinctions.15: 이수변 is a conventional shape-name; the meaning clue is 얼음.
importantDistinctions.163: 邑 is the settlement radical used in right-side 阝; it is not 阜.
importantDistinctions.170: 阜 is the hill radical used in left-side 阝; it is not 邑.
importantDistinctions.74: 月 uses the moon clue; meat-related forms are classified separately under 肉130.

5.note: Keep the conventional name 새 을, but do not mistake the name for the bird radical; use curved stroke and the second heavenly stem as the short learning clue.

172.note: 隹 denotes the short-tailed bird category. Short tail is not the same as a small-sized bird.

171.note: The traditional name 미칠 이 refers to reaching, not the unrelated Korean sense of going mad.

156.note: Keep the traditional radical name 달아날 주; the short clue also accommodates the modern Chinese verb 走, to walk.
